JOINT ADVISORY FX-2026-01 (FICTIONAL TEST DOCUMENT)
Fixture Spider Targets IT Help Desks

This advisory is synthetic test data for cti-to-detection-agent. Every name, address and hash in it is invented.

Summary
Fixture Spider (also known as Octo Fixture and UNC0000) is a financially motivated group. The actors call IT help desks while posing as employees to get password and MFA resets [T1566.004]. They then flood users with MFA prompts until one is accepted (T1621).

Technical details
After gaining access, the actors install remote access software such as AnyDesk and ScreenConnect to keep a foothold. They exploited CVE-2023-4966 on unpatched appliances in two intrusions.

Reporting
Report incidents to report@cisa.gov or visit cisa.gov/report. Organisations can also contact their regional field office, which coordinates with national partners and shares anonymised findings with other affected sectors so that defenders everywhere benefit from each report.

Indicators of compromise
The following infrastructure was observed in March 2026:
- hxxps://helpdesk-reset-fixture[.]net/login (phishing page)
- 198.51.101[.]7 (command and control)
- support-sso-fixture[.]com (lookalike domain)
- SHA-256: 0f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f00f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0 (loader)

Mitigations
Require phishing-resistant MFA for every account that can reset credentials. Verify callers through a known channel before resetting passwords or enrolling new MFA devices. Restrict remote access software to an approved list and alert when anything else is installed. Patch internet-facing appliances within days, not weeks.
